fields.title: Drivers Instead of Bill Line Items
fields.keyTakeaway: Expenses are forecasted from product drivers rather than read from the bill, and the condition for this is resource tagging introduced in advance.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The bill grew by 30% in a quarter. Why and what to do about it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A bill read as a list of services gives no answer: it shows that compute got more expensive, but not due to which product decision. Investigation takes weeks and usually ends in targeted savings instead of understanding.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: The [[cost-model|cost model]] links expenses to [[cost-driver|drivers]]—metrics they depend on.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Typical drivers and what depends on them:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: The model is built once: each major bill item is tied to a driver, resulting in a formula. Then expenses are forecasted from the product plan rather than guessed.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: Condition for viability—[[tagging|resource tagging]]. Without tags on resources, the bill remains general and cannot be broken down. Tagging is introduced once and requires discipline: each new resource is tagged upon creation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: [[cost-allocation|Cost allocation]] is the next step: attributing expenses to teams, features, or clients. It enables calculating [[cost-to-serve|cost to serve]] and finding features with disproportionate costs.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Rule of thumb: **80% accuracy is sufficient.** Trying to break down every penny consumes more than it saves.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text:
Compute       = 0.0033 RUB × requests
Storage       = 26 RUB × GB
Traffic       = 5.7 RUB × GB
SMS           = 4.2 RUB × sends
Geocoding     = 0.3 RUB × calls
Acquiring     = 1.2% × turnover
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The 30% growth was broken down in an hour: 12%—audience growth (expected), 11%—event volume growth after adding new ones, 7%—data accumulation.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The second item was unexpected: the analytics team added 14 new events, and volume doubled. No one calculated the cost upon addition because the event seemed free.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Introduced a rule: a new event in a high-frequency scenario is accompanied by an annual cost calculation. Out of the next 20 proposed events, 6 were dropped.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The model becomes outdated when architecture changes. It is worth reviewing during major changes rather than maintaining continuously.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Expenses are forecasted from product drivers rather than read from the bill, and the condition for this is resource tagging introduced in advance.
